cards.title: Index Selection and PDT Definition via Time-Kill and In Vivo Models
cards.claim: Time-kill studies provide preliminary insight into the PK/PD index (e.g., AUC/MIC vs. T>MIC) most likely to predict efficacy, but are not a universal mandatory prerequisite for all linkage analyses if in vivo data is sufficient. Nonclinical PD targets (PDTs) are defined as the exposure levels associated with specific bacterial effects: net stasis (0 log10 drop), 1 log10 drop, and 2 log10 drop. The selection of the appropriate index (AUC/MIC, Cmax/MIC, or T>MIC) is guided by the bactericidal pattern observed in time-kill studies (concentration-dependent vs. time-dependent).
conditions: Applicable for defining the primary PK/PD index for subsequent PTA/CFR analysis.

For an MIC-normalized index, use a strain-matched MIC with method, units and measurement context. Use time-kill data to characterize temporal killing or inform index choice when that question requires it; EMA antimicrobial-development guidance separately recommends time-kill studies and relevant MIC distributions for the development package. A full MIC distribution is not required solely to normalize a single-strain index.
PDTs must be defined for specific pathogens or groups of pathogens relevant to the indication.
required_inputs: Time-kill study data showing concentration-dependent or time-dependent killing patterns.
In vivo efficacy data (CFU counts) at various exposure levels.
Definition of the observation window for effect measurement.
limitations: Time-kill data informs index choice but does not replace the need for in vivo validation of the index.
PDTs derived from animal models require translation to human exposure; species differences in PK and binding must be accounted for.
A PDT is not automatically applicable to all strains; strain-specific MICs and intrinsic resistance mechanisms (e.g., capsule) may alter maximal effect (Emax).
cards.downstream_use: Select the primary PK/PD index for PTA modeling. Define specific PDT values (e.g., fAUC/MIC for stasis) to be used as targets in Monte Carlo simulations.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Exposure-response linkage to strain/MIC, effect window, baseline, assay and matrix

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
